classification.tone: Stylized, tense, sensual, and increasingly unhinged

evaluation.positioning_hook: A couples therapist’s affair with her patient’s husband turns into a manipulative power game when the wife reveals she’s been orchestrating the seduction all along.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise is immediately legible and built around sex, marriage, and professional betrayal, which gives it a clear adult audience and a strong curiosity engine. It’s more targeted than four-quadrant, but the hook is clean enough to sell on premise and conversation value.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The central engine lands early: Pau’s flirtation at the party, the reveal that Oliver is Mare’s husband, and the later reversal that Mare has been steering the whole thing. The story is easy to explain in a sentence or two, and the escalation is built on a very clear irreversible choice.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Pau is a strong lead because she’s composed, erotic, ashamed, and increasingly cornered, while Mare and Oliver each carry a distinct charge that keeps the triangle alive. The characters are most compelling when they’re in conflict, and the script gives them enough contradiction to sustain a feature.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script commits to a high-wire erotic-thriller premise with a therapist, a married couple, and a consent/power reversal that keeps mutating. The final turn into Mare’s orchestration, the hidden camera, and the therapy-session-as-hostage setup show real confidence in escalation and provocation.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The script keeps tightening the noose: party encounter, secret affair, professional exposure, surveillance, blackmail, and then physical entrapment. Each major sequence adds a new pressure point, and the ending confrontation in Pau’s office gives the story a strong, escalating payoff.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The idea of a couples therapist being seduced into the very marriage she’s meant to treat feels fresh and instantly playable. The later reveal that the wife has been directing the whole affair gives the premise a nasty inevitability that makes the concept stick.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The Manhattan high-rise, therapy office, private equity/law world, and Hudson weekend-house material create a specific upper-middle/upper-class social ecosystem with clear status games. The world is not sprawling, but it has enough moneyed texture, professional etiquette, and domestic architecture to feel story-generating.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a distinct erotic-psychological tone: polished surfaces, operatic music, clinical language, and sudden bursts of humiliation and violence. The contrast between elegant domesticity and raw sexual power play gives it a recognizable identity.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: Beneath the thriller mechanics, the script keeps circling marriage fatigue, desire, control, ambition, and self-erasure. The final divorce turn and Pau’s last-image self-possession suggest a deeper story about reinvention, not just scandal.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The Pau/Oliver/Mare triangle is the engine, but Anders and Sylvie add useful pressure and contrast, especially once the marriage and the Hudson weekend become part of the trap. The relationships are strongest when they cross-contaminate one another, which the script uses well.

Friday Cafe, Nespresso, LinkedIn, Instagram, academia.edu, Tanqueray, Maker’s, and Four Seasons are all named on the page.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model; best suited to festival-to-platform or adult genre theatrical positioning.

cost.note: Contemporary and largely contained, but the Manhattan, Hudson, hotel, law-office, and restaurant footprint plus night work and a car crash push it above microbudget.

cast.note: The script depends on three adult leads with very specific chemistry and a credible teenage son, but it does not require a large ensemble.

location.note: The story moves through multiple upscale interiors and a Hudson getaway, with enough company moves to matter but no period builds or remote terrain.

content.note: Explicit sex, coercive power play, blackmail, choking, blood, and a car crash place it firmly in adult-only territory.

rights.note: The script uses several named brands and a specific Mozart aria, but there are no real-person life-rights dependencies.

strengths.what_it_means: A buyer can understand the engine in one breath: a therapist sleeps with her patient’s husband, then discovers the wife has been steering the affair. That kind of clean, adult hook is ideal for streamer genre buyers and producers looking for a conversation-starting thriller with a clear audience lane.
strengths.evidence: The party meet-cute, the hotel-room affair, and the later reveal that Mare orchestrated the setup all lock the concept in place.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Pau is a showcase lead role.
strengths.what_it_means: The part gives an actress glamour, repression, erotic charge, panic, and moral collapse in one package, which is exactly the kind of performance vehicle that can attract serious talent. Mid-career dramatic leads and actors looking to pivot into prestige genre would see a juicy, scene-rich centerpiece here.
strengths.evidence: Pau moves from controlled therapist to adulterous participant to terrified target to hard-eyed survivor, with the office, hotel, and bathroom sequences all built around her reaction.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The erotic power reversal is the engine.
strengths.what_it_means: The script keeps flipping who is in control, which gives the story a built-in escalation pattern and a strong hook for adult genre buyers. That dynamic is catnip for directors and audiences who want sex scenes to carry plot, not just heat.
strengths.evidence: Mare’s reveal that she directed Oliver, the hidden camera in Pau’s office, and the final hostage therapy session all turn desire into strategy.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The world has affluent social texture.
strengths.what_it_means: The Manhattan penthouse, private equity/law marriage, therapist office, and Hudson weekend house create a polished upper-class ecosystem where every room has status pressure. That gives the film a premium sheen that helps it play above a standard affair thriller and makes it attractive to buyers who want sophistication with pulp.
strengths.evidence: The anniversary party, the law office, the Upper East Side apartment, and the Hudson house all feel like extensions of the same social class.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The tone is controlled and operatic.
strengths.what_it_means: The Mozart motif, the elegant interiors, and the increasingly unhinged sexual and psychological behavior create a distinctive tonal signature that a director can lean into hard. That blend is especially attractive to filmmakers who like prestige surfaces with taboo material underneath.
strengths.evidence: Opera opens the script and returns throughout, including the final image of Pau masturbating to it in her new apartment.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The ending leaves a strong aftertaste.
strengths.what_it_means: The final movement gives the story a clean emotional landing without sanding off the danger, which helps the film feel complete rather than merely sensational. Buyers like endings that resolve the central triangle but still leave a charged image in the audience’s head.
strengths.evidence: Pau divorces Anders, starts therapy, and then sees Mare and Oliver outside the wine bar before the final solo image.

whats_special.headline: FIXATION is a sleek adult thriller with a killer premise: a couples therapist falls into an affair with her patient’s husband, only to discover the wife has been orchestrating the whole seduction. It’s built for actors, loaded with status, sex, and psychological reversal, and it has the kind of premium, conversation-starting hook that can travel in the marketplace.

lead_characters.name: Dr. Paulina Cuevas Ström
lead_characters.hook: Pau is polished, intelligent, and deeply self-managed, the kind of woman who can transform herself in an elevator from tired anonymity into social elegance in seconds. Under that control is a restless hunger she keeps trying to intellectualize away, and the script lets us watch her composure become the very thing that traps her.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Julianne Moore in *May December* or Nicole Kidman in *Birth* — a woman whose surface control slowly gives way to obsession, shame, and self-recognition. It gives an actress the full range: erotic tension, professional authority, humiliation, panic, and a final hard-earned reclamation of self.

lead_characters.name: Meredith Adler
lead_characters.hook: Mare is all poise, appetite, and strategic intelligence, a woman who reads as glamorous until you realize she is the most dangerous person in the room. She’s ambitious, sexually commanding, and emotionally exacting, with the unnerving ability to turn vulnerability into leverage.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase space of Rosamund Pike in *Gone Girl* — a character who weaponizes intelligence, charm, and performance to control the room. Actors who want to play icy precision with flashes of erotic menace will chase this because it gives them dominance, wit, and a late-film reveal of real ferocity.

lead_characters.name: Oliver Ramos
lead_characters.demographics: Male · 40s · polished, attractive, finance/private equity type
lead_characters.hook: Oliver is charming in a way that never quite feels innocent, a man whose flirtation reads as social ease until it becomes clear he uses desire as a tool. He’s the script’s most slippery figure: needy, controlled, performative, and capable of sudden aggression when his status is threatened.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of morally unstable male lead Jake Gyllenhaal played in *Nightcrawler* — a charismatic surface with something predatory and self-justifying underneath. It gives an actor the chance to move from seduction to menace to collapse without ever losing the audience’s attention.

lead_characters.name: Anders Ström
lead_characters.hook: Anders is the quieter counterweight in Pau’s life: affectionate, slightly stalled, and more observant than he first appears. He reads as the stable husband until the script reveals he has his own calculations, resentments, and capacity for manipulation.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of understated marital role that gave Michael Stuhlbarg so much to do in *A Serious Man* — a man whose calm exterior can suddenly reveal deep emotional pressure. Actors who excel at dry intelligence and wounded restraint will see a lot to play here.

lead_characters.name: Sylvie Porter
lead_characters.hook: Sylvie is the social lubricant of the opening world: funny, frank, and casually miserable in a way that makes the party feel lived-in. She gives the film its first note of adult marital candor and helps establish the class and social code Pau moves through.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of sharp supporting hostess role that lets an actor do the *Big Little Lies* style of breezy social comedy with a bite underneath. It’s a compact part that can still land memorable lines and establish the film’s adult tone immediately.

lead_characters.name: Bill Porter
lead_characters.hook: Bill is the kind of rich husband who thinks he’s charming because he’s harmless, which makes him useful as a social mirror for the film’s marriage games. He’s not the engine, but he helps define the world’s casual entitlement and sexual drift.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a good character turn in the vein of Richard Jenkins in *The Visitor* or a lighter *Succession* patriarch-adjacent role — a man whose vanity and obliviousness are funny until they aren’t. It gives a seasoned actor easy authority and comic texture.

lead_characters.name: Jackson
lead_characters.hook: Jackson is the office foil: younger, socially easy, and used to being around Pau’s competence without understanding its cost. He functions as a pressure valve and a witness, which makes him useful whenever the script needs the outside world to register Pau’s unraveling.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of supporting role that works for an actor with the easy, naturalistic charm of a *The Bear* ensemble player — someone who can make a few scenes feel lived-in and real. It offers clean, grounded contrast to the film’s heightened central triangle.

lead_characters.name: Fidan
lead_characters.hook: Fidan is one half of the couple Pau treats, and she gives the therapy scenes emotional specificity through her bluntness and recovery history. She helps show Pau’s professional competence before the story starts eating away at it.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of sharply observed supporting role that lets an actor do the intimate realism of a *Marriage Story* secondary character in miniature. It’s a concise but credible part for someone who can make therapy dialogue feel personal rather than functional.

lead_characters.name: Kunter
lead_characters.hook: Kunter is the more emotionally exposed half of the therapy couple, carrying worry, resentment, and tenderness in the same scene. He gives the film an early example of how love and suspicion can coexist in the same room.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor the grounded marital pain of a Noah Baumbach supporting part — enough emotional truth to matter, enough specificity to feel real. It’s a useful showcase for someone who can play hurt without overplaying it.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to make sex feel like strategy and strategy feel like danger.
director_appeal.fit_profile: Established indie or prestige-genre directors with at least one feature under their belt, especially those who work well with actors and can sustain tension in contained interiors. This material rewards filmmakers who care about performance, visual control, and the slow escalation of psychological humiliation into physical threat.
director_appeal.detail: The movie gives a director a clean three-hander engine, elegant production design, and a chance to stage erotic scenes that actually move the plot. It’s especially attractive to directors who like polished surfaces cracking under pressure and who can make a single room feel like a battlefield.

buyer_appeal.lane: Premium streaming / adult erotic thriller lane
buyer_appeal.detail: The script can be packaged around three strong adult leads and does not require VFX-heavy execution, which makes it viable for a director-driven greenlight. The erotic-thriller lane remains a recognizable streamer and festival-to-platform play, and the Manhattan/Hudson setting gives it upscale export appeal.

considerations.area: The final act has room to sharpen the external objective.
considerations.detail: The script’s last movement is strongest when Pau is reacting to Mare and Oliver’s control games; a next pass could foreground one concrete endgame she is actively trying to achieve once the blackmail and surveillance escalate. That would make the final stretch feel even more propulsive without changing the core premise.

considerations.area: The therapy scenes can carry more story pressure.
considerations.detail: Several office sessions do important character work, but a few of them play as elegant exchanges of diagnosis and response; one lever would be to let each session turn on a fresh piece of information or a sharper tactical move. That would keep the professional scenes feeling like plot engines, not just atmosphere.

considerations.area: The Hudson section can be streamlined.
considerations.detail: The getaway material does useful work on marriage and exposure, but the script already has a strong pressure-cooker in Manhattan and the office. The version of the story where one Hudson sequence absorbs the function of another would protect momentum and keep the feature feeling taut.

considerations.area: The brand and music references are specific.
considerations.detail: Mozart, the named cafes, the hotel, and the social-media platforms all help texture the world, but they also create a modest clearance layer. A producer can keep the specificity while planning early for music and brand substitutions where needed.

considerations.area: The adult leads need chemistry that can pivot.
considerations.detail: The script asks Pau, Mare, and Oliver to move from flirtation to humiliation to threat to intimacy, often in the same scene. Packaging should prioritize performers who can play seduction and control without flattening either side of the triangle.
